title: Fresh Blender 5.2 directional holdout for the frozen Material-owner one-sided curvature candidate
question: On unseen Blender 5.2 rasters, owner boundaries, material signals and rigid projective trajectories, does the frozen factor-1 Material-owner one-sided second-difference candidate recover left-, right-, top- and bottom-missing curvature support without accepting a neither-side negative control or violating the frozen risk, quality, identity, fallback and coverage gates?
decisionRole: confirmatory generalization test of D12.12-D1; it may promote factor 1 only as a bounded opaque rigid-planar candidate and cannot establish production readiness

scientificClassification.freshMeasurement: All six fixtures, rasters, object and material tokens, material coefficients, camera states, owner trajectories and formal output paths are unseen in D12.9-H1, D12.11-I1 and D12.12-D1.
scientificClassification.frozenIntervention: The inflation factor is exactly 1. The Material Index, structural, Q30/Q24, risk threshold, reconstruction order, fallback and verdict gates are frozen before any H1 source tool or render output.
scientificClassification.negativeResultValue: A safety, directionality or coverage failure is retained as evidence against generalization; fixture parameters, denominators and gates may not be repaired post-render.

requirements: This specification, every new formal tool path, the preflight root and the formal root are absent when preregistration begins.
This exact specification is committed and pushed before any new formal or preflight tool byte exists.
All eight formal tools are frozen in a later commit before any formal root or formal EXR exists.
A zero-render preflight may construct all scenes, inspect Blender RNA and exercise synthetic branch fixtures, but may not render, create the formal root or emit a formal measurement.
Formal output consists of 24 new Blender 5.2 Cycles CPU renders; no D12.9, D12.11 or D12.12-D1 EXR or adapter array is a measurement input.
The D12.11 and D12.12-D1 formal Git trees remain identical before and after H1.
No fixture, transform, signal, directional class, token, threshold, denominator, attack family or verdict mapping may change after this commit.

sceneContract.construction: fresh factory state; opaque analytic tessellated rectangular owners with continuous Generated object-local emission; no source blend, external asset, image texture, light, transparency, deformation, simulation, motion blur, depth of field, compositor or denoiser

purpose: bilinear Material support with neither horizontal outer difference

ownerTokenContract.objectIndexNegativeControl: Both analytic owners in each fixture deliberately share the same Object Index; Object Index must remain byte-stable but may not be a decision input.
ownerTokenContract.materialIndexDecisionInput: Exact finite float32 equality to the declared compiler-assigned integer token.

projectionOracle.cameraConvention: Blender camera looks along local -Z; camera coordinates are transpose(R_camera_XYZ)*(world-cameraLocation)
projectionOracle.currentSurface: cast the current pixel-center ray through every declared bounded owner plane and select the nearest positive-depth hit
projectionOracle.previousSurfacePoint: inverse current owner transform maps the hit to owner-local coordinates; previous owner transform maps the same local point into world space
projectionOracle.predictedPreviousDepth: negative previous-camera Z of the transformed current local surface point
projectionOracle.independence: analyzer and auditor implement scalar Euler XYZ, pinhole projection, bounded ray-plane intersections and rigid transforms without importing bpy, a consumer or analyzer helper

structuralContract.registeredCurrent: finite current RGBA/depth/vector/material; alpha>0.999; declared nonzero current Material Index; analytic current owner exists
structuralContract.bilinearSupport: all four previous taps are in bounds, alpha>0.999 and have exact Material Index equality to the current analytic owner token
structuralContract.predictedDepth: bilinearly sampled previous Depth matches transform-predicted previous-camera depth within max(1,predictedPreviousDepth)/1024
structuralContract.currentInterior: current pixel and every current neighbor within Chebyshev radius 2 have the same exact Material Index and alpha>0.999
structuralContract.fallback: every registered pixel outside accepted copies current float32 RGBA exactly
forbidden: Object Index equality as owner identity
analytic truth or current/future RGB as a consumer decision input

frozenCandidate.name: MATERIAL_OWNER_ONE_SIDED_D2_FACTOR_1
horizontalRule: For each bilinear row, compute the left Q30 second difference only when x0-1 has the same Material Index and valid alpha, and the right difference only when x0+2 does.
Use max(left,right) when both exist, the single absolute difference multiplied by exactly 1 when only one exists, and reject when neither exists for a required row.
verticalRule: For each bilinear column, compute the top Q30 second difference only when y0-1 has the same Material Index and valid alpha, and the bottom difference only when y0+2 does.
Use max(top,bottom) when both exist, the single absolute difference multiplied by exactly 1 when only one exists, and reject when neither exists for a required column.
frozenCandidate.riskFormula: riskQ30 = ceil(2*(Fx*(2^24-Fx)*Mx + Fy*(2^24-Fy)*My)/2^48)+512, saturated to uint32 maximum independently per RGB channel
frozenCandidate.acceptance: recomputed structural and radius-2 domains, common bilinear Material support, horizontal and vertical curvature support, and max RGB riskQ30 <= 131072 inclusive
frozenCandidate.reconstruction: four-tap previous RGBA bilinear graph ((v0*w0+v1*w1)+v2*w2)+v3*w3 in binary64 with one final float32 cast
frozenCandidate.fullStencilIdentity: where the entire symmetric 4x4 Material/alpha stencil is valid, risk, accepted and reconstructed bytes must equal an independently recomputed D12.11 symmetric baseline

directionalMeasurementContract.analysisOnly: Directional classes and measurement regions are derived after decisions and may never influence accepted, risk or reconstruction arrays.

classes.LEFT_MISSING_RIGHT_AVAILABLE: both bilinear rows lack a valid left outer tap and have a valid right outer tap; both vertical columns retain full top+bottom support
classes.RIGHT_MISSING_LEFT_AVAILABLE: both bilinear rows lack a valid right outer tap and have a valid left outer tap; both vertical columns retain full top+bottom support
classes.TOP_MISSING_BOTTOM_AVAILABLE: both bilinear columns lack a valid top outer tap and have a valid bottom outer tap; both horizontal rows retain full left+right support
classes.BOTTOM_MISSING_TOP_AVAILABLE: both bilinear columns lack a valid bottom outer tap and have a valid top outer tap; both horizontal rows retain full left+right support
classes.NEITHER_HORIZONTAL_AVAILABLE: common four-tap Material support is valid but at least one required row has neither a valid left nor right outer tap
classes.STATIC_FULL_STENCIL_CONTROL: camera and both owners are transform-identical across frames; the full symmetric stencil is the primary control domain

directionalMeasurementContract.measurementRegion: inclusive normalized rectangle applied only by the independent analyzer after a directional class has been derived

coverageGates.denominator: all recomputed radius-2 current Material-owner cells; no support or risk reject may be dropped
forbidden: claiming directional recovery excuses a 0.97 or 0.95 failure

requiredFamilies: bound D12.11 and D12.12-D1 parent byte and formal-tree mutations
spec, tool, runtime, environment, process-roster and operation-count mutations
source EXR, source report, adapter payload, adapter report and multipart roster mutations
Material Index zero, reuse, swap, undeclared and out-of-range mutations
Object Index divergence from the shared negative control and Object/Material channel substitution
projection, vector sign/order, depth oracle and structural reason-order mutations
left, right, top and bottom outer-tap owner/alpha substitutions
directional-class, region and one-sided eligibility injections
factor value or label mutations and hidden factor search
Q30/Q24 scale, second difference, max, numerator, ceil, allowance, saturation and inclusive-threshold mutations
accepted-set, risk-underbound, quality, alias and false-invalid injections
current RGB decision dependence and future RGB leakage
fallback, static-control, coverage denominator and per-owner retention mutations
cross-language, repeat, result, audit, execution, envelope and receipt chain mutations
attacks.independence: The auditor may use Python standard library and NumPy but may not import Blender modules, a source tool, adapter, consumer, analyzer or runner. Every counted attack mutates an isolated in-memory semantic payload and must trigger at least one named gate.

decision.supportedWhen: Every hard, directional, negative-control, coverage, process, repeat, cross-language, audit and attack gate passes in both clean repeats.
decision.boundedWhen: Every hard safety, identity, directional and neither-side gate passes, but at least one unchanged 0.97 cell or 0.95 owner coverage gate fails.
decision.directionFailureWhen: Hard identity and safety gates pass, but one or more frozen directional fixtures fails its minimum witness, accepted-count or 50% directional-acceptance gate, or the neither-side negative control lacks a witness.
decision.rejectedWhen: Any parent, freshness, runtime, process, source, repeat, cross-language, token, projection, structural, risk-underbound, quality, alias, false-invalid, fallback, static, neither-side acceptance, audit-totality or attack gate fails.
decision.promotionBoundary: Even the supported verdict promotes factor 1 only to the next separately preregistered nonplanar, lit or production-pass holdout. It does not authorize production compiler integration.

nonClaims: This experiment does not provide a mathematical error bound for arbitrary rendered functions.

The fixtures are opaque, rigid, planar, emission-only analytic surfaces and do not establish behavior for curved or deforming geometry, transparency, hair, volumes, lighting, shadows, denoising, motion blur or depth of field.
Pixel error gates do not establish perceptual importance or cinematic quality.
The shared Object Index is a negative control; success cannot be attributed to Object Index ownership.
A source-bound visualization or measurement-region mask may not influence a temporal decision.
No verdict retroactively changes D12.9-H1, D12.11-I1 or D12.12-D1.
